add.title: Add environment
add.body: Name it now, or let the first agent name it after its host.

name.label: Name (optional)
name.helper: Leave this empty to use the host's name when the first agent connects. You can rename it later.

rotate.title: Show install command
rotate.description: Generate a new join token and its install command.
rotate.alert: This replaces the previous token. Install commands you copied earlier stop working. Agents that are already enrolled aren't affected.

step2.title: Install the agent
step2.body: Run one of these on a swarm manager or on a standalone host. TierPlan detects which it is.

helper.swarm: Run it on any manager node. It creates a Docker secret for the join token and starts the agent as a global service, so nodes you add later enrol by themselves.
helper.standalone: Run it on the host. It starts the agent container with the Docker socket mounted.
helper.composeSwarm: Save this as `tierplan-agent.yml` and run `docker stack deploy -c tierplan-agent.yml tierplan-agent`.
helper.composeSwarmSecret: Create the secret first with the command in the file's first line.
helper.composeStandalone: Save this as `tierplan-agent.yml` and run `docker compose -f tierplan-agent.yml up -d`.

update.heading: Update the join token on this swarm
update.helper: Docker secrets can't be edited, so this command removes the old secret and adds the new one.
update.serviceName: It is for an agent installed with the command, whose service is named `tierplan-agent`. If you installed from the stack file, the service is named after your stack, such as `tierplan-agent_tierplan-agent`; change the name in the command to match.

install.secretNotice: This command contains a secret. It starts with a space so shells that ignore space-prefixed commands keep it out of history. Once your hosts are enrolled, rotate the token from Settings.

trust.label: Server certificate
trust.public: Trusted through public certificate authorities. This command carries no pin.
trust.publicNote: The agent keeps the self-signed pin it receives when it connects, so going back to self-signed needs no reinstall.
trust.unverified: This certificate isn't trusted through public certificate authorities, so this command carries no pin and the agent can't verify it.

waiting.body: This updates by itself when the agent connects.
waiting.slow: Still waiting? Check that the host can reach {{url}}, then look at the agent's log: `docker logs tierplan-agent` (standalone) or `docker service logs tierplan-agent` (swarm).
